description.p: img-fp finds copies of the same picture, even when they are not the same file. It compares images by their local features rather than by one hash of the whole picture, so it still finds a match after an image has been re-encoded, resized, cropped, rotated, recoloured, or placed inside a slide, collage or screenshot. Every match is checked against the pixels before it is shown.

ul.li: Exact copies under different names or in different folders
The same image saved again at a different size, quality or format
An image inside a larger one: a slide, a collage, a page, a screenshot

description.p: Pick folders and start the scan, then go through the groups and choose which images to move to the Trash. For each image the scan suggests whether to keep or delete it, never deleting the only copy of what a picture shows; nothing is marked until you ask. A copy can be compared with its group's reference, with the part each shows of the other outlined.
JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, BMP, TIFF, HEIC, AVIF, JPEG XL and more are read. The command-line tool is included as well: flatpak run --command=img-fp io.github.danielnara24.img-fp --help

description.p: A cut-off copy of a photo is recognised as part of the intact one, an icon file holding several sizes is no longer offered for deletion, a cache setting pointed at another file no longer overwrites it, and caches left by older versions are removed.
Copies of logos, icons and other pictures with little detail are found in folders full of other photos, and a damaged copy of a photo is no longer kept in place of the intact one.

A photo stored sideways with a rotation tag is recognised as the same picture as an upright copy, folders of many copies of one photo are compared much faster, and the Trash no longer takes an image whose kept copy was deleted while the confirmation was open.
Comparing pictures is faster, most of all in folders holding many copies of the same photos. What is found is unchanged.

Two pictures get the same answer whatever else is in the folders being scanned, so a small folder and a whole library agree. Photos that only share a part, such as a distant mountain both show, are no longer grouped together.

Detail added to a plain area, such as a person painted on a wall, now counts when pictures are compared. A rescan no longer reads identical copies again, and the window can reuse a scan made in the terminal.
Motion Photos and pictures with a gain map are kept rather than deleted for their still copy. The cache opens faster, and a rescan where nothing changed skips the matching.

A moved or renamed file is analysed again, so two files can no longer be taken for each other. Of copies with the same pixels, the one with a colour profile, camera details or more colour depth is kept.

Files deleted in another program are noticed before anything is moved to the Trash, and files on drives without a Trash can be deleted permanently. img-fp no longer offers itself as the program that opens folders.
Damaged and empty files are reported with their cause, a library inside the scanned folder is handled, and the large view can show a picture at its actual size.
The progress bar follows the time left, measured as the scan goes.
